newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian rates should not be cut - Access.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian rates should not be cut - Access.

text.p: Consultancy firm Access Economics said on Wednesday it believed the Reserve Bank (RBA) should not cut official interest rates again in the current cycle.
"We agree inflation prospects are excellent, and that activity is currently quite soft," Access Economics said in its September quarter report.
"Yet the outlook for the world economy continues to improve.
"Linked to that substantial resource investment in Australia is providing a solid base to activity. Accordingly, if it were up to us, we would not cut Australian cash rates again in this cycle."

Access said the possibility of an interest rate cut remained quite high, although rate hikes were likely to follow in late calendar 1997. "We expect rate rises will be back on the agenda by late 1997," it said.
Australian financial markets now widely expect the RBA to cut interest rates between late October and early November after it left rates unchanged on Wednesday.
Interest rates were last changed on July 31, when they were cut by 0.5 percentage points to 7.00 percent.
Access said it expected the economy to turn upwards in late 1997.
"Although short term activity will be weaker than Treasury has it, an upturn is coming," Access said.

It said this would be powered by a recovery in the housing sector, robust resource investment, and good growth in both the United States and Japan. "With all these factors coming together, the long run of good news on Australian inflation may peter out in mid to late 1997," it said.

The RBA has an underlying inflation target of an average of two to three percent over the course of 1996/97. The Australian government, in its August 20 budget, set a growth target of 3.5 percent for 1996/97. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730
